I graded `s2` and saved the verdicts and feedback for each answer to `grades/0001-s2.json`. I didn't grade `s1`.

| Item | Verdict | Main point |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model outputs a request to use a tool. |
| q3 | Wrong | A stuck agent needs a step limit; letting it run longer isn't a safeguard. |
| q4 | Partial | 4 model calls is right, but your reason says the model runs the tools. |
| q5 | Correct | You explained both what happens to the result and why. |
| q6 | Partial | The model uses each tool's description, not just its name. |

**Summary:** Riley, you know what makes an agent, what the model outputs when it wants a tool and how the result gets back to it.

The main thing to fix is who runs the tools. **The model only asks; the program runs them.** Your q2 answer says the model sends a request, but your q4 reason says it runs the tool itself. Also work on when a loop should stop (q3) and what a tool description contains: its name, what it does and the inputs it takes (q6).

**Next step:** trace the laser cutter request from q4 again. Label each step "model" or "program", and mark where a step limit would stop the loop. You can send me your trace to check.

I also added two learning records: [what you showed you understand](learning-records/0003-tool-results-return-to-the-model.md) and [what's still open](learning-records/0004-open-tool-execution-and-stopping.md). I updated `NOTES.md` so we check the open points before moving on to context and memory.
